title: Stepped degradation plans for load shedding and priority graphs
content:
Summary:
This note captures a proposal for stepped (aka phased) graceful degradation across the Redwood inference control plane. Goal is to define deterministic, observable, and testable behavior when demand exceeds capacity or when region-level failures occur. Key ideas: priority graphs (user/request priorities mapped to capacity tiers), explicit load-shedding tokens, cost-aware eviction policies, and a clear multi-region spillover sequence.

Why a new plan?
- Existing fallback docs focus on model family fallbacks and simple regional spillover. We need an operator-friendly scheme that composes: routing policy, admission control, runtime eviction (KV cache), and model-variant substitution in ordered steps.

Assumptions and constraints:
- Customers pin model versions; platform may substitute to compatible model-variants (semantically similar, lower-cost) only under configured policies.
- Latency SLOs vary by tier (Gold: p95 <= 200ms, Silver: p95 <= 400ms, Bronze best-effort).
- We cannot silently change output semantics for Gold tier unless explicitly allowed by customer policy.
- Each region exposes capacity signals: available-GPU-cores, queue-depth, avg-token-latency, and prewarmed-kv-warmth.

Glossary (short):
- Priority graph: directed graph that maps request classes (e.g., interactive, batch, embeddings) to preference order of execution paths and model variants.
- Tiered capacity: logical buckets (Gold/Silver/Bronze/Spot) claimed against different pools (dedicated, shared, burst).
- Stepped degradation: pre-defined stages applied sequentially as pressure increases.
- Admission token: ephemeral grant issued by control plane to a request indicating it can enter runtime.

Principles:
1) Determinism: given same inputs and capacity signals, routing should make the same decision for identical requests.
2) Observability: every step records event with reason-code (e.g., STEP_2_SHED_LOW_PRIORITY, STEP_3_USE_QUANT) plus metric annotations.
3) Sanity-first: never violate explicit customer isolation/SLA checks; fallbacks must respect model pinning policies.
4) Testability: each step is toggleable in platform test harness and in chaos-scenarios.

Stepped degradation stages (recommended default):
Stage 0 - Normal: route to requested model variant in-region.
Stage 1 - Soft throttle: enforce per-customer concurrent limit and reduce batch sizes incrementally. Return 429-limited with retry-after when hard limits hit.
Stage 2 - Priority shedding: drop / deprioritize low-priority request classes (background jobs, low-cost embeddings), preserve Gold interactive traffic. Emit shed events to billing/CS pipelines.
Stage 3 - Model-variant substitution: for Silver/Bronze eligible requests, substitute to quantized or smaller model variant (explicit mapping in model-catalog). Customer-level overrides allowed.
Stage 4 - Cross-region spillover: route accepted requests to adjacent region with capacity; use region-affinity scoring to minimize latency increase (see routing heuristic below).
Stage 5 - Burst fallback pools: allow execution in burst pools that may increase cost or use preemptible instances; warn user and tag trace with cost-increase.
Stage 6 - Hard-fail: return controlled degradation responses (short-circuited canned answer / offline-opt-out) only for extremely-low-priority classes.

Priority graph example (text DSL):
# request-class definitions
class interactive {priority: 0; allowed_tiers: [Gold, Silver]; model_variants: [v1-fp16, v1-8bit, v1-quant]; preserve_semantics: true}
class embed-bulk {priority: 2; allowed_tiers: [Silver, Bronze, Spot]; model_variants: [embed-small, embed-quant]; preserve_semantics: false}
class rerank {priority: 1; allowed_tiers: [Gold, Silver]; model_variants: [rerank-large, rerank-quant]; preserve_semantics: true}

# edges indicate fallback preference with cost estimate tags
interactive -> interactive:v1-8bit [cost_delta: -0.45, latency_delta: +0.1]
interactive:v1-8bit -> interactive:v1-quant [cost_delta: -0.65, latency_delta: +0.05]

Routing heuristic (multi-region):
Score(region) = latency_penalty*predicted_rtt + cost_penalty*estimated_unit_cost + affinity_penalty*not_primary_region + capacity_bonus*(free_slots/total_slots)
Route to region with lowest Score above a minimum capacity threshold. If no region meets threshold, consider Stage 5 burst pools or Stage 6 fail.

Admission control and tokens:
- Central control plane issues short-lived admission tokens with metadata: request-class, allowed-stage, issuance-region, expiry.
- Runtime checks token on request ingress; token contains allowed model-variants. If runtime cannot satisfy token (e.g., model not loaded), it returns a token-failure event and control plane re-evaluates (fast re-route or issue negative ack).

Eviction and KV cache policies:
- Eviction is cost-aware: evict entries belonging to low-priority classes first or entries that yield low reuse. Use an LRU-weighted-by-priority strategy.
- Implement a gentle KV eviction: mark cold-entries as candidates and delay eviction until Stage 3 to avoid unnecessary model warmups in earlier soft-throttle stages.

Observability / telemetry hooks (must exist for each step):
- Event stream keys: degradation.stage, reason_code, affected_request_classes, model_variant_swapped, source_region, target_region, token_id.
- Metrics: shed_rate_by_class, avg_token_latency_by_variant, admission_token_rejects, cross_region_routed_pct, cost_delta_estimate.
- Alerts: if Stage 2 shedding > 2% of incoming for >5m, page oncall. If cross-region routing increases average p95 by >20% for Gold, run mitigation playbook.

Operator playbook (quick run):
1) Detect: automated alert triggers (shed rate spike or capacity drop).
2) Triage: check control-plane capacity graph, per-region queue depths, and model load percentages.
3) Run stepwise rollback knobs: disable Stage 3 substitutions for pinned customers, increase Silver concurrency limits by 10%, or enable extra burst pool.
4) Communicate: post a short Slack message to #platform-incident with high-level impact and ETA.
5) Postmortem data capture: preserve event logs for the incident window and mark all decision steps with trace ids.

Testing and validation matrix:
- Unit tests for policy DSL evaluation, edge-case permutations (pinned+stage3 allowed=false).
- Integration tests: inject synthetic region outages and assert behavior sequence: Stage 1 -> 2 -> 4 as configured.
- Load tests: ramp QPS to observe deterministic stage transitions under different customer mixes (80% interactive vs 80% bulk).
- Chaos experiments: random preemption of burst pools and ensure control-plane loops to Stage 6 without customer data loss.

Backward-compatibility and customer controls:
- Customers may opt out of any stage beyond Stage 1 via account-level flag (e.g., no-variant-substitution=true).
- For pinned models, control plane must honor the pin and either route to a different region (if allowed) or return explicit 409 with guidance.

Open questions/risks:
- Cost attribution when Stage 5 uses expensive burst pools: how to bill and display to customer in near real-time?
- Semantic equivalence: for cases where substitution changes output (e.g., different tokenizer behavior), what automated checks can we run to avoid regressions?
- How to encode model-compatibility and output-quality guarantees into the model catalog metadata so Stage 3 policies can be safely automated?

Next steps (actionable):
- Prototype a policy-evaluator microservice that reads priority graphs and emits admission tokens (owner: Liam). Target alpha test in staging (date +4w).
- Add telemetry keys and dashboard templates (owner: Maya).
- Draft customer-facing opt-out docs for substitution and cross-region routing (owner: Evan).

References and notes:
- See linked artifacts for initial implementation PR and Confluence draft.
- Slack thread: #platform-degrade (ref PLAT-2221) contains early feedback from solutions eng.

Appendix: Example incident timeline (short)
- 09:02: autoscaler failure reduces GPU capacity in us-west by 40%
- 09:03: control plane triggers Stage 1 (soft throttle) and records event
- 09:04: heavy background embed traffic gets shed (Stage 2) — shed_rate_by_class spikes
- 09:06: majority of accepted Silver requests are substituted to 8-bit variants (Stage 3)
- 09:08: when Stage 3 substitution reaches threshold, cross-region routing activates to us-east for Gold traffic (Stage 4)
- 09:20: operators enable burst pool for critical customers to restore headroom
- 09:45: autoscaler recovers; control plane gradually steps back from Stage 5 -> Stage 3 -> 1 -> 0

This doc is intentionally operationally focused and meant to be a working draft for engineering alignment. Comments welcome — please add inline notes or attach test results to PLAT-2221."
